controls.title: Segment networks by risk and function
controls.statement: Place systems into defined security zones based on business criticality, sensitivity and trust, and separate IT from OT where applicable.
controls.risk: A compromise of one device could spread widely and interrupt critical services if the network provides broad, flat access.
controls.scope: Internal networks, cloud networks, management networks, security zones, IT and OT boundaries.
controls.examine: Compare current diagrams, asset criticality and data flows with implemented zones, routing, firewalls and authentication boundaries.
controls.interview: Ask architects and service owners how zone placement and permitted communications are decided and reviewed.
controls.test: From representative zones, attempt authorised benign connections to approved and prohibited destinations and verify enforcement and logging.
test_steps: Select representative user, server, management, guest, cloud and OT zones and identify the approved trust level and permitted services between them.
From authorised test hosts in each source zone, attempt benign connections to approved destinations and verify the expected application and identity restrictions.
Attempt prohibited lateral and cross-zone connections, including a high-risk management path, and confirm default denial without an alternate route.
Trace allowed and denied attempts to monitoring and compare observed reachability with current diagrams and rule documentation.
controls.expected: Assets are placed in justified zones and prohibited cross-zone paths are blocked while approved business flows remain available.

mappings.basis: The networking procedure requires segmentation by criticality and trust with communications constrained to controlled paths.
Requires IT systems to be separated from OT systems through physical or logical segmentation.
Requires important assets to be segmented into security zones based on cybersecurity requirements.
Requires a secure network architecture addressing segmentation, least privilege and availability.
ASD describes segmentation and segregation design practices but the document is guidance rather than an auditable control.
mappings.excerpt: Network segmentation partitions a network into smaller networks, while segregation develops and enforces rules controlling communications between hosts and services. Effective measures must be planned, enforced, monitored and unable to be bypassed.

controls.title: Control traffic across network boundaries
controls.statement: Route communications through managed boundary controls and allow only authenticated and authorised traffic needed for defined business functions.
controls.risk: Uncontrolled network paths could let an attacker move between systems, extract information or bypass monitoring.
controls.scope: External interfaces, internal zone boundaries, gateways, firewalls, proxies and other managed network controls.
controls.examine: Inspect data-flow approvals, boundary rules, gateway designs, rule reviews, monitoring and exceptions.
controls.interview: Ask network and service owners how each allowed flow is justified and how obsolete or emergency rules are removed.
controls.test: Sample allowed and denied flows across external and internal boundaries and verify source, destination, service and logging behaviour.
test_steps: Select external and internal boundary rules covering inbound, outbound, management and inter-service traffic, including temporary exceptions.
Independently verify source, destination, protocol, port, application, identity and time conditions against the approved business requirement.
Generate authorised allowed traffic and closely related prohibited traffic to confirm exact enforcement, state handling and absence of a broader shadow rule.
Confirm both outcomes are logged with usable context and that expired, unused or duplicate rules are removed through the review process.
controls.expected: Traffic crosses boundaries only through managed controls and only for current authorised flows, with blocked attempts visible to monitoring.

mappings.basis: Requires gateways between security domains in the source scope.
Requires monitored managed interfaces, separated public components and boundary-protection devices aligned to architecture.
Requires network protections to be defined and enforced for selected asset types according to risk and priority.
Requires network intrusion detection on enterprise assets where appropriate; it can observe boundary traffic but does not define or restrict allowed flows.

controls.title: Maintain and test network architecture
controls.statement: Keep network architecture and data-flow diagrams current and test that the design remains resilient after system, threat and business changes.
controls.risk: Unknown connections and outdated designs could hide single points of failure or paths attackers can use to reach critical systems.
controls.scope: Network architecture records, diagrams, reviews and resilience testing for in-scope environments.
controls.examine: Compare diagrams and architecture decisions with discovered connections, current assets, review records and resilience test results.
controls.interview: Ask architects how material change triggers review and how operational failure and attack scenarios influence design.
controls.test: Sample network segments and data flows against diagrams, then review evidence from a recent failure, isolation or penetration test.
test_steps: Select network segments, gateways, cloud networks and important data flows and compare observed routes and controls with approved current diagrams.
Trace recent architecture changes from approval into diagrams, firewall policy, routing, monitoring and recovery documentation.
Review a recent failure, isolation or penetration test and verify it exercised critical boundaries, alternate paths and the assumed blast radius.
For one controlled path, disable or isolate the component in a test window and confirm traffic fails safely or follows only the documented resilient route.
controls.expected: Architecture records match the environment, material changes receive review and testing demonstrates that critical functions remain protected.

mappings.basis: Requires a documented cybersecurity architecture covering IT and OT systems and networks.
Requires periodic and trigger-based evaluation of conformance to the cybersecurity architecture.
Requires current network architecture diagrams and annual or significant-change updates.
ASD provides architecture design and validation context but the document is guidance rather than an auditable control.
mappings.excerpt: Resilient networks restrict lateral and vertical movement to authorised requests. Network design must support business requirements, be regularly reviewed and be tested through exercises, penetration tests and simulated failures.
